still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, with oral initial doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) at $149/month.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
The CMS Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model still pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay, and still requires ≥80% refill adherence and ≥5% loss at 6 months, with a 12-month lockout on lapse.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.

population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 52M of ~268M US adults are currently on an incretin (19.4%). Age check: 0.20×10.5 + 0.33×19 + 0.24×31 + 0.23×16 ≈ 19.5. Income thirds 26/19.5/12.5 average ≈ 19.3. The bottom third is flat, not rising: five states dropped Medicaid obesity coverage and the 2029 importation crackdown roughly doubled gray-market prices, so gains from cheaper orals were cancelled out. Cycling arithmetic: ever 27.5% − current 19.4% = 8.1 pp of adults (~21.7M) who used and are off now. Coverage-driven churn rose (employer drops, Medicaid exits, the Wegovy pen shortage of Sep 2029–Mar 2030, Medicare lockouts), so ~38% of current users are restarters (0.38×19.4 ≈ 7.4 pp) and ~22% of those currently off had cycled before (0.22×8.1 ≈ 1.8 pp): (7.4+1.8)/27.5 ≈ 33%. Of the ~21.7M off-drug ever-users, about 7M stopped for a coverage or supply reason rather than a side effect. Payer mix of the 52M current users: diabetes-, cardiac-, OSA- or MASH-coded coverage across all payers ~23M; employer obesity coverage ~6.5M (down from 8M); Medicare Continuity Model obesity-only ~2.2M; Medicaid obesity (14 states) ~1.1M; TRICARE active-duty readiness ~0.1M; brand cash via TrumpRx or direct ~14M (up from 10M, mostly orals); gray market ~5.1M (down from 6M). These sum to 52.0M. Pediatric: ~0.9% of under-18s (~0.65M), almost all aged 12+. Under-12 use is still specialist-only and off-label. About a third of US children now live in a household where an adult is on the drug. The never-users with obesity who cannot afford $149+ are the largest untreated group: roughly 35M adults with BMI ≥30 have never used one.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the Continuity Model is unchanged at $245/$50 with adherence and response conditions. Enrolment grew to ~2.2M obesity-only beneficiaries as boomers aged in: 2.2M × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.5B/yr, about 60% above the ~$4B/yr CBO baseline. CMS answered by tightening documentation audits, not by cutting the rate. Medicaid: after 2029–30 budget cycles squeezed by the 2025 reconciliation law's financing changes, five states ended obesity coverage, leaving 14 states and ~1.1M enrollees. Gross cost is 1.1M × $245 × 12 ≈ $3.2B/yr, of which the federal share at a ~65% blended FMAP is ≈ $2.1B. Nine of the 14 now attach adherence waivers. TRICARE: from Jan 2030, active-duty members in body-composition remediation get coverage through the Metabolic Readiness Program (~100k enrolled; ~100k × ~$230 × 12 ≈ $0.28B/yr).
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ generic semaglutide brands at ~$8–40/month, and generic oral semaglutide has been on sale there since 2028. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and most of Southeast Asia have injectable generics. Canada formalised its bulk-export restriction on generic semaglutide in 2029 after US border-state buying. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: The price shock comes through supply and channels, not brand list prices. (1) In Aug 2029 Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs reached Indian and Chinese peptide API and finished injectables, and CBP ended personal-importation discretion for injectable peptides. Telehealth import prices rose from $60–120 to $110–200/month and the two largest importers stopped US shipping. (2) An FDA warning letter at Novo's North Carolina fill-finish site put higher-dose Wegovy and Ozempic pens on the shortage list from Sep 2029 to Mar 2030. About 1.5M users were forced onto a lower dose, a different brand or nothing. The listing briefly made 503B compounding lawful again, which ended when the shortage was declared resolved. (3) Five states withdrew Medicaid obesity coverage. Brand cash prices: injectable semaglutide $199, Zepbound $249–299, Foundayo and Wegovy pill from $149, and Novo's oral amycretin (launched Jul 2030) at $349. Retatrutide stays at $399 for starting and middle doses, but from Jan 2030 Lilly priced the top maintenance doses at $449, saying launch-term pricing had ended. Because gray import prices now overlap the $149 brand orals, many former gray users moved to TrumpRx pills, so the gray market shrank as it got dearer. Research-peptide retatrutide ($150–250) is the most resilient gray channel. Employer weight-management coverage: 44% (2028) → 40% (2029) → 36% (2030, Business Group on Health). New starts are ~60% oral.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin dual agonist, daily oral (amycretin oral, Novo; approved Jun 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, Sep 2028)
moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder in adults, no BMI requirement (semaglutide, Sep 2030)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers
low-dose 'sober-curious' use by heavy but non-dependent drinkers, now easier to prescribe after the AUD label
research-peptide retatrutide in gym and 'recomposition' communities
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
anecdotal cannabis, gambling and compulsive-shopping use in addiction-medicine practices
drugs.pipeline_note: Oral parity is realised by Novo's oral amycretin. It was filed Feb 2029 and approved Jun 2030 (16 months), after phase 3 showed ~22% mean loss at 72 weeks, in line with injectable tirzepatide. It launched Jul 2030 at $349 cash. It does not match retatrutide's ~29%, which remains the ceiling. The needle barrier is gone for everyone except those chasing maximal loss. Semaglutide AUD: the phase 3 programme read out Jan 2029 with fewer heavy-drinking days than placebo and benefit regardless of BMI. The sNDA was filed Apr 2029 and approved Sep 2030 (17 months), the first incretin indication with no weight criterion. Survodutide: filed Jun 2029, under FDA review with a decision expected 2031. MariTide (monthly): phase 3 complete, BLA filed Oct 2030, not on the market. Global incretin market ~$135B (2030). Lilly is still the largest player; Novo regains US new-start share through oral amycretin.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading side-effect cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin's GI profile is similar to injectables at maintenance and worse during titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction, including persistence after discontinuation (mass-tort litigation)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on-drug is established pharmacology. Gastroparesis persisting after stopping is not established: cohort data conflict, and diagnosis by gastric-emptying study is inconsistent. MDL 3094 (E.D. Pa.) passed ~42,000 filed claims by mid-2030, up from a few thousand in 2025. Growth came from TV and social advertising aimed at the ~22M people who have stopped, plus claims tied to retatrutide and gray-market product. The first bellwether (May 2030) returned a $14M failure-to-warn verdict against Novo, now on appeal. The second ended in a defense verdict. Perioperative aspiration claims are a growing sub-docket.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added class-wide language on severe GI reactions and pre-procedure holding to all incretin labels (Mar 2030). No finding that gastroparesis persists. Anaesthesia society holding guidance is unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; highest with retatrutide.

Still no causal confirmation in long RCTs and absolute risk is low. Pancreatitis and a handful of pancreatic-cancer claims are now consolidated in MDL 3094, which keeps the question in the news even though the evidence has not moved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; in the MDL; no pancreatitis verdict yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Bone-density association in women over 60 on long-term use replicated in a second US cohort (2029). Causation versus weight-loss effect unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide and amycretin labels recommend resistance exercise and protein counselling. Endocrine Society suggests baseline DXA for women over 60 on high-efficacy agents.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; a small number of NAION claims sit in the MDL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The AUD phase 3 programme, with neuropsychiatric monitoring, found no excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still unquantified. The AUD trials measured craving and drinking days but no validated anhedonia or hedonic-capacity scale. Reduced wanting is now on-label as the therapeutic effect in two addiction indications. The complaint lives mainly in 0mg-movement and anti-pharma media, so clinicians discount it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. The AUD label carries standard neuropsychiatric monitoring language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Coverage- and supply-driven stops (employer drops, Medicaid exits, the 2029–30 pen shortage, Medicare lockouts) remain the commonest cause of discontinuation. Real-world regain is roughly half of lost weight within a year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; it still underpins Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE adherence conditions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More reports at retatrutide-level intake reduction and in older adults.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; professional societies recommend baseline and annual labs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~33% of ever-users have now cycled. The FDA Sentinel cycling study's interim report (2030) is descriptive only. The earliest adolescent starters approach five years in 2031.

FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~7,000 by mid-2030. Research-peptide retatrutide now dominates the count. The import crackdown cut Indian generic volume but pushed some users toward unlabelled peptide vials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion stands, except during the 2029–30 shortage window. CBP ended personal-importation discretion for injectable peptides (Aug 2029). Research-peptide sites face sporadic warning letters.

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A US claims replication (2029) found a smaller hazard ratio (~1.3) with wide intervals. Confounding by diabetes duration is still unresolved. Absolute excess is still estimated at a few per 1,000 person-years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded in 2029 with 'olfactory disorders, uncommon' added to EU semaglutide product information. FDA still reviewing; no US label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Dose-related, mostly mild, more frequent at the $449 top maintenance doses.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~31% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~5–6% from 2026 and sugary drinks ~4–5%. Protein, fibre, small-format and 'companion' SKUs keep growing. A contrary niche has appeared: 0mg-branded 'whole-fat, full-plate' products (butter, sourdough, raw-milk-adjacent dairy) sell well in Tennessee, Idaho and Texas grocery chains, but they are a rounding error nationally. Midwest private-label snack plant closures continue at a slower pace.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down another ~4% over two years and beer down ~2%. Heavy-drinker decline is the named driver in 10-Ks. The Sep 2030 AUD approval brings no immediate volume change, but distillers' risk factors now cite it and analysts model a further 2–3% decline by 2033. Non-alc keeps growing. Tobacco cessation demand is up and cigarette volume decline has steepened modestly.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat, tickets are supported by small plates and protein add-ons, and half-portion menus are standard at national chains. Buffets keep closing. Bars lose late-night trade. Supper clubs and 'feast' dinners marketed to 0mg crowds do well in Nashville and Austin.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting with further Torrid and DXL closures. Mainstream retailers carry wider size runs to serve regainers and cyclers, and return rates stay elevated. 0mg-aesthetic brands (linen, workwear, unretouched campaigns) are a small growth niche.

fitness.state: Strength and 'muscle-preservation' studios keep growing, many with oral-GLP-1 telehealth bundles. CrossFit-style boxes in the South split into on-drug and 0mg gyms. Big-box cardio gyms are flat.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 36%. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, OSA and MASH codes. About 1 in 4 large self-funded employers now run BMI or adherence premium differentials. The Sep 2030 AUD label creates a new question: parity rules for substance-use treatment may stop plans from excluding semaglutide prescribed for AUD, and benefits consultants expect obesity-excluded patients to be recoded. Pharmacy trend ~7%.

pharma.state: Volume growth continues, now led by orals. Lilly is still the largest; Novo recovers US new starts with oral amycretin after a damaging fill-finish shortage. Litigation reserves appear in both firms' filings. Tariffs hit Indian generic makers' US gray channel, not their legal export markets.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness after 40 in affluent suburbs still reads as being on a drug. The new move is to say you are not: '0mg' pins, bio lines and gym-bag patches claim a body as unassisted. Strangers can no longer read a larger body at all; it might be refusal, a lockout or a lapsed employer plan.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers have hardened further. Coded-coverage and insured professionals are at the top. The cash middle buys $149–299 orals. The bottom third sits flat at 12.5% on-drug, squeezed by Medicaid exits and dearer gray imports. 0mg has a class edge of its own: its most visible faces are thin, affluent, often Christian millennial mothers and CrossFit men, for whom 'unmedicated' advertises self-made discipline. Fat-liberation organisers in Atlanta and Oakland openly distrust it.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first half portions are the norm in GLP-1 households. 0mg households make a point of the full table: Sunday dinners photographed whole, sourdough, butter, second helpings as testimony. Church potlucks in middle Tennessee now advertise themselves as 0mg events.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: '0mg' is a common Hinge and Bumble profile label in Nashville, Austin and Boise, and 'on it' remains one in New York and LA. Mixed couples describe negotiating dinners, drinking and, after the AUD label, whether one partner's drinking is a 'condition'. Lower desire is still mentioned anecdotally and rarely attributed.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Every appetite with a label (food, nicotine, now alcohol) is officially treatable. The 0mg movement answers that appetite is the self, and that mastering it unassisted is the point. That is a moralised mirror of medicine's claim, not a rejection of control. It shares enemies with fat liberation, MAHA and 'Made Whole' congregations but shares a theory with none of them.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Still unmeasured. The AUD trials, the largest neuropsychiatrically monitored incretin trials yet, used craving scales and drinking diaries but no hedonic-capacity endpoint. With reduced wanting on-label twice over, any flattening is read as the treatment working. 0mg media talk about 'chemically calm' people constantly, which makes the claim politically coded and clinically ignorable.
interior_life.framing: Treatment and character. Quieter wanting is called recovery, maturity, discipline, or in the military 'readiness'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Army units in the Metabolic Readiness Program report fewer alcohol-related incidents and body-composition failures. Commanders credit discipline and the programme, not mood. Police departments with officer GLP-1 benefits report anecdotally fewer use-of-force complaints, which nobody has analysed. Sales managers still grumble about 'flat' closers off the record.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Late-night bar culture keeps thinning: trivia nights, bowling leagues and dive-bar music in mid-sized cities. High-sensation formats such as loud live shows, endurance events and ice baths keep their vogue. 0mg feast dinners and 'appetite' supper clubs are a recognisable scene in Nashville. Some songwriters there market their records as unmedicated.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Anecdotes of being 'content, not hungry' for partners persist, discussed on couples-therapy podcasts and in 0mg sermons. There is still no clinical literature.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measured effect on participation. 'They're sedating the troops' becomes a 0mg and MAHA-influencer line after the Army programme launches, which keeps the effect from being studied by anyone seen as neutral.

state.regulatory_posture: Split and getting more so. The FDA is fast on approvals (oral amycretin, the AUD label) and on the shortage-window exceptions. Trade and border agencies are now tough on importation, a shift driven by tariff policy, not drug safety. MAHA voices in the administration praise 0mg while TrumpRx still sells $149 pills.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No civilian mandate. Price-controlled public access is unchanged in Medicare at $245 and shrinking in Medicaid (14 states). TRICARE pays for active-duty readiness use. The military programme is voluntary on paper; the alternative for a soldier who keeps failing body-composition standards is separation.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare and nine Medicaid waivers require ≥80% refill adherence and ≥5% loss at 6 months, with a 12-month lockout. About 1 in 4 large self-funded employers run health-contingent BMI surcharges ($50–100/month), waived on biometric proof or connected-pen adherence. The Army programme logs monthly weigh-ins and pen or pill-bottle sensor data in unit readiness systems. Tennessee's 2029 Unmedicated Workers Act bars state-regulated employers and plans from requiring GLP-1 use or penalising refusal; ERISA plans and federal employers are exempt.
state.workforce_or_military: From Jan 2030 the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program offers TRICARE-covered tirzepatide, semaglutide or orals to active-duty members in body-composition remediation (~100k enrolled). Accession waivers now need only 3 months of off-drug weight stability, down from 6. The FAA continues to clear pilots on approved incretins after a stable-dose period. Several large city police and fire departments (Houston, Phoenix and others) cover GLP-1s for 'fitness-for-duty'. FMCSA guidance lets truck drivers with OSA document tirzepatide-treated improvement in medical certification.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs on Indian and Chinese peptide API and CBP's end of personal-importation discretion sever most of the India-to-US gray channel. India redirects exports to the Gulf, Africa and Latin America. Canada restricts bulk export of generic semaglutide. Lilly and Novo onshore more fill-finish capacity, which is how a single US plant failure became a national shortage.

events.event: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs extend to Indian and Chinese peptide ingredients, and CBP ends personal-importation discretion for injectable peptides. Telehealth importers' generic semaglutide jumps from about $60–120 to $110–200 a month and the two largest stop US shipping. The same month, Business Group on Health finds employer weight-loss coverage has fallen to 40%; it reaches 36% in 2030.

Some 30,000 people rally in Nashville under '0mg' banners. Weeks later Tennessee passes the Unmedicated Workers Act, which bars state-regulated employers and plans from requiring or rewarding GLP-1 use but does not reach large self-funded employers.

The Pentagon launches the Metabolic Readiness Program. It offers TRICARE-covered GLP-1 drugs to active-duty members who fail body-composition standards, with monthly weigh-ins logged to readiness records, and cuts the off-drug stability requirement for recruits from six months to three.

A federal jury in Philadelphia returns a $14M verdict against Novo Nordisk in the first bellwether trial of the GLP-1 gastroparesis litigation, which now holds about 42,000 claims; a second bellwether ends in a defense verdict weeks later.
FDA approves Novo's oral amycretin, a daily pill that produced about 22% average weight loss in trials, in line with injectable tirzepatide; it launches in July at $349 a month cash.
FDA approves semaglutide for moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder in adults with no weight requirement, its first indication not tied to body size.

open_tensions: The AUD label has no BMI floor, while employers excluding obesity use may be barred by substance-use parity rules from excluding AUD use. Whether 'alcohol' becomes the new coverage code for people dropped from obesity coverage, and whether the administration enforces parity, decides the next two years of access.

Mass-tort scale litigation over gastroparesis and pancreatitis is running on weak causal evidence, just as oral parity and the AUD label widen the exposed population. A bellwether reversal or a large settlement could move labels and prices more than any trial.

The military now treats the drug as readiness infrastructure, while the Medicare lockout and Medicaid exits push civilians through forced cycles nobody has studied. 0mg politics in Tennessee and Texas want both rolled back and has no answer for soldiers facing separation.

Reward blunting is still unmeasured while the drug is licensed to suppress two cravings and handed to soldiers and police. The first adolescent cohort crosses five years in 2031, the year US generics are expected.

prose.headline: The Pill Caught Up, the Coverage Didn't: 52 Million Americans On, 22 Million Off, and a Movement Wearing '0mg'
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about 52 million American adults, nearly one in five, take an incretin drug. More and more of them take it as a pill. In June the FDA approved Novo Nordisk's oral amycretin, which takes off about as much weight as a weekly tirzepatide shot. For most new patients the needle is now optional, and six in ten new starts are oral. Lilly's injectable retatrutide is still the ceiling at nearly 30 percent loss, and its top doses now cost $449 a month in cash.

The pill did not make the drug cheaper for the people at the bottom. Employers kept retreating: just over a third still pay for weight loss alone, and the rest cover the drug only for diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea or liver codes. Five states dropped Medicaid obesity coverage when their budgets tightened. In August 2029 the cheap route closed. Tariffs reached Indian peptide ingredients, and customs ended the personal-importation tolerance that had let telehealth firms ship $60 generics. Gray-market prices nearly doubled. Many of those buyers moved to the $149 TrumpRx pills, which became the more affordable option. Others stopped. Then a warning letter at one North Carolina plant put Wegovy pens on the shortage list for six months, and about a million and a half people found their dose unavailable. The bottom income third, at about 12 percent on the drug, has not moved in two years. About 22 million adults have used one of these drugs and are off it now; a third of everyone who ever started has stopped and restarted at least once.

Medicare still pays $245 and still checks refills and weigh-ins, locking out anyone who lapses. Enrolment has grown faster than budgeted, and CMS has responded with audits rather than cuts. The Pentagon has made the drug part of its readiness system. Since January, soldiers who fail body-composition standards can take a TRICARE-paid GLP-1 under monthly weigh-ins logged to unit records, or face the old separation process. Big-city police departments cover it for fitness for duty, and truckers use tirzepatide to keep their medical cards.

In September semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder, the first indication with no weight requirement. Benefits consultants are now asking whether plans that excluded obesity can exclude addiction treatment under parity rules. Reduced craving is now on the label for nicotine and for alcohol. The old talk of people feeling flat on the drug has become a political accusation, and no one has measured it.

The accusation now belongs to the 0mg movement. It began in Nashville among church-going millennial mothers and CrossFit men, and spread to Boise and Austin as pins, profile badges, butter-heavy supper clubs and photos of full tables. Its claim is that a body made without medicine is your own. Some of its most visible faces are thin, which makes fat-liberation organisers in Atlanta uneasy. Tennessee passed a law barring state-regulated employers from requiring the drug, which does not reach the large self-funded employers that charge BMI surcharges.

In Philadelphia, about 42,000 people are suing over gastroparesis and pancreatitis. The first jury awarded a plaintiff $14 million and the second sided with Novo. The science has not moved much: delayed stomach emptying on the drug is real, and a stomach that stays damaged after stopping is unproven. Lawyers are advertising to the 22 million people who have stopped. Europe now lists loss of smell as an uncommon effect of long-term use; America is still reviewing it.

Snack volumes are down another couple of points, spirits are down again, bars close earlier and buffets keep shutting. Nothing has collapsed. The country is lighter, more sober, more monitored, and sorted by who pays for the drug.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Specialist Marcus Bell weighs in at 0600 at Fort Campbell, in socks, on the scale by the orderly room. Sergeant Pruitt reads the number aloud and taps it into the tablet. Down four pounds. The tablet already knows whether Marcus took Sunday's tirzepatide; the pen told it.

"Readiness," Pruitt says, the way he says everything.

PT, chow. He eats eggs and half the potatoes. The other half sits there and he doesn't mind it.

At lunch he calls his mother in Hopkinsville. Her Medicaid stopped covering it in March. She had been on the Indian stuff from the website until it got to $180, and now she's on the $149 pill and says it makes her queasy in the mornings. She asks if the Army will cover her. He says no, Ma.

Kayla picks him up at five in her mother's truck. There's a 0mg sticker on the tailgate and flour on her jeans; she sells sourdough at the Clarksville market on Saturdays. They drive to her church's potluck. A banner over the folding tables says ALL WHO HUNGER. He fills a plate to be polite. Her uncle watches him and says, "Uncle Sam's appetite or yours?"

Later, at the barracks, his roommate's birthday. A bottle of Fireball goes around. Marcus passes it on without thinking and then notices he didn't think about it. Last year he would have been the one who brought it.

Kayla texts: you seemed far away tonight.

He types, just tired, deletes it, types, guess I'm growing up, and sends that.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Weeks later Tennessee passes the Unmedicated Workers Act, which bars state-regulated employers and plans from requiring or rewarding GLP-1 use but does not reach large self-funded employers.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a bill passing 'weeks' after an October rally is too fast. Tennessee's legislature normally sits January to April, and no special session or other vehicle is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Enrolment grew to ~2.2M obesity-only beneficiaries as boomers aged in
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: aging-in alone does not explain a ~47% jump in two years. The Continuity Model's adherence, response and lockout conditions should cap enrolment growth, and no uptake mechanism is given.

least_plausible_claims.quote: EMA PRAC concluded in 2029 with 'olfactory disorders, uncommon' added to EU semaglutide product information.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a label change within about a year of the signal review opening, on a replication with a smaller hazard ratio (~1.3), wide intervals and unresolved diabetes-duration confounding, is faster and firmer than the evidence supports.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse. Forced cycling (about 7M coverage- or supply-driven stops), the flat 12.5% bottom third, Medicaid exits and the Army's weigh-in and pen-sensor logging with separation as the alternative drive autonomy and inequality. Epistemic is highest: reward blunting is unmeasured and politicised, and is now on-label as the therapeutic effect for two cravings. The 0mg split and the litigation add cohesion and public-health costs, but nothing is catastrophic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible and traceable. Employer coverage falls 44→36%. The shock_up price path appears as tariffs, the pen shortage and the $449 top retatrutide dose, though brand injectable cash prices stay flat, so the shock is modest. The AUD indication, GI/pancreatic MDL with a bellwether, oral amycretin parity, 0mg culture, the Pentagon programme and 'unrecognised' personality layer are all present. mechanism: most changes have chains (tariffs to gray prices to TrumpRx pills; FDA label language to litigation), but the Tennessee law's speed, the Medicare enrolment jump and the quick EMA label change (claims 1–3) are asserted more than shown. magnitude: all figures sit inside the envelope (19.4% on drug, 27.5% ever) and reconcile. The age and income checks, the 52.0M payer mix, the 33% cycling arithmetic, the Medicare $6.5B, Medicaid $3.2B/$2.1B and TRICARE $0.28B all multiply out, and approval timings of 16 and 17 months respect the 12-month rule.
rationale.generativity: The Marcus Bell scene shows rather than explains: the weigh-in, the pen that reports to the tablet, the half-eaten potatoes, the 0mg church potluck, the mother on Medicaid and gray-market pills, and the Fireball he did not think about. Together with the 0mg supper clubs, the MDL lawyers and the police and trucker programmes, it implies many characters and scenes. The ending's 'growing up' line closes the interior-life thread.

least_plausible_claims.quote: roughly 35M adults with BMI ≥30 have never used one
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: with 27.5% of adults ever having used a drug and roughly 40% of adults at BMI ≥30, the never-user obesity pool is closer to 70M+ than 35M. The figure does not reconcile with the population numbers and understates the 'largest untreated group'.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Police departments with officer GLP-1 benefits report anecdotally fewer use-of-force complaints, which nobody has analysed.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a specific behavioural outcome is asserted from the drug with no causal chain. It is hedged as anecdotal, but it is an unsupported convenient link to the reward-blunting theme.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral parity is realised by Novo's oral amycretin. It was filed Feb 2029 and approved Jun 2030 (16 months), after phase 3 showed ~22% mean loss at 72 weeks
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude/mechanism: amycretin was only in phase 3 in 2028, so a 72-week readout and a filing by Feb 2029 is very tight. An oral peptide matching tirzepatide-level loss is an optimistic leap, although it stays inside the envelope's 12-month rule.

rationale.badness: The two-tier system hardens: the bottom third is flat at 12.5%, five states drop Medicaid coverage, there are ~22M off-drug ever-users, and ~7M stopped for coverage or supply reasons. Autonomy erodes through adherence lockouts, BMI surcharges at 1 in 4 large self-funded employers, and an Army programme whose alternative is separation, with pen-sensor data logged to unit records. Reward blunting is now on-label as therapy in two addiction indications, is still unmeasured, and is politically coded, which hurts epistemics. Material harms are moderate rather than catastrophic, so this reads as a recognisably harder society.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised. The shock_up price path comes through tariffs, the pen shortage and the $449 top-dose tier, which is a mild expression of the driver. The shortage and tariff events sit slightly uneasily against market_shock 'none'. mechanism: Most changes have shown chains, such as tariffs raising gray prices, gray users moving to $149 pills, and audits rather than rate cuts in Medicare. The police use-of-force line is asserted without a chain (claim 2), and oral amycretin's timeline is aggressive (claim 3). magnitude: Adoption (19.4%), ever-used (27.5%), the income thirds, payer mix (sums to 52.0M), Medicare and Medicaid spending, TRICARE spending and cycling arithmetic all reconcile, and approval timings obey the 12-month rule. The one real reconciliation miss is the ~35M never-used obesity figure (claim 1).
rationale.generativity: The Fort Campbell vignette shows rather than explains: the scale, the pen that reports to the tablet, half the potatoes, the mother on Medicaid and then on the $149 pill, the 0mg sticker and the sourdough, the ALL WHO HUNGER banner, the Fireball passed on, and 'guess I'm growing up'. Many characters and scenes are implied: the 0mg potluck, military readiness, the litigation and the supper clubs. Daily life has strong texture, and the vignette carries the reward-blunting theme through implication.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo regains US new-start share through oral amycretin.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism fails: the pill launched in July 2030 at $349 cash, against $149 Foundayo and Wegovy pills. It matches tirzepatide rather than beating it, and it has under six months on the market. A share recovery in that time is asserted, and the parent's own CagriSema precedent (modest uptake because it did not beat tirzepatide) points the other way.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Because gray import prices now overlap the $149 brand orals, many former gray users moved to TrumpRx pills, so the gray market shrank as it got dearer.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a tidy offsetting story, but it sits awkwardly beside the stated rise in FDA adverse-event reports (4,000 to 7,000), research-peptide retatrutide being 'the most resilient gray channel', and a bottom income third that stays flat at 12.5%. A $110–200 import is not cheaper than a $149 pill for most of those users, so the shrinkage looks convenient.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Weeks later Tennessee passes the Unmedicated Workers Act, which bars state-regulated employers and plans from requiring or rewarding GLP-1 use
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the act is enacted within weeks of a first rally, and its content is inconsistent across fields. The event says it bars 'requiring or rewarding' use, while state.conditioning_or_surveillance says it bars requiring use or 'penalising refusal'. Those are different laws.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder, more stratified version of 2028. Employer coverage falls to 36%, five states drop Medicaid, the bottom third is flat at 12.5% against 26% for the top, and about 7M people were stopped for coverage or supply reasons. Autonomy suffers from soldiers facing separation, 1-in-4 employers running BMI surcharges, and pen and bottle sensor data feeding readiness systems. The epistemic score reflects reward blunting being unmeasured while two cravings are now on-label, and the 'sedating the troops' framing keeping it politically coded. The harms are real but moderate: no collapse, and the safety signals are contested.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible: +1.6pp adoption exactly, employer retreat 44→40→36, AUD approval, MDL gastroparesis litigation, oral amycretin, 0mg culture, the military programme, and an unrecognised personality layer. 'shock_up' is realised only through tariffs, a shortage and the $449 top retatrutide dose, with brand cash prices otherwise flat. The Novo plant failure and tariffs also sit uneasily next to 'market_shock: none'. mechanism: most changes have chains (tariffs and CBP lead to dearer imports and then to the shortage and Medicaid exits). Weak points are the claimed Novo share recovery, the gray market shrinking while getting dearer, and the inconsistent Tennessee law between the event and the conditioning field (see the three listed claims). The EMA label added on a weaker replication (HR ~1.3) is also somewhat fast. magnitude: on-drug 19.4% and ever-used 27.5% are inside the envelope, and the income thirds bracket the national figure. The age check, payer mix (sums to 52.0M), cycling arithmetic (~33%), Medicare ($6.5B), Medicaid ($3.2B gross, $2.1B federal) and TRICARE ($0.28B) all reconcile. Approval timings (amycretin 16 months, AUD 17 months, survodutide and MariTide not approved) obey the rules, and there is no US generic.
rationale.generativity: The Fort Campbell vignette is concrete: the weigh-in, the pen that reports to the tablet, the mother on Medicaid who has dropped to a $149 pill, the 0mg sticker, the potluck banner, the Fireball he passes without noticing. It shows reward blunting without naming it. The world also implies many other scenes: AUD parity fights, 0mg supper clubs, police fitness-for-duty benefits, Medicaid-exit households, and the bellwether trials.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Weeks later Tennessee passes the Unmedicated Workers Act, which bars state-regulated employers and plans from requiring or rewarding GLP-1 use but does not reach large self-funded employers.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a bill passing 'weeks' after an October rally is too fast. Tennessee's legislature normally sits January to April, and no special session or other vehicle is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Enrolment grew to ~2.2M obesity-only beneficiaries as boomers aged in
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: aging-in alone does not explain a ~47% jump in two years. The Continuity Model's adherence, response and lockout conditions should cap enrolment growth, and no uptake mechanism is given.

least_plausible_claims.quote: EMA PRAC concluded in 2029 with 'olfactory disorders, uncommon' added to EU semaglutide product information.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a label change within about a year of the signal review opening, on a replication with a smaller hazard ratio (~1.3), wide intervals and unresolved diabetes-duration confounding, is faster and firmer than the evidence supports.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse. Forced cycling (about 7M coverage- or supply-driven stops), the flat 12.5% bottom third, Medicaid exits and the Army's weigh-in and pen-sensor logging with separation as the alternative drive autonomy and inequality. Epistemic is highest: reward blunting is unmeasured and politicised, and is now on-label as the therapeutic effect for two cravings. The 0mg split and the litigation add cohesion and public-health costs, but nothing is catastrophic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible and traceable. Employer coverage falls 44→36%. The shock_up price path appears as tariffs, the pen shortage and the $449 top retatrutide dose, though brand injectable cash prices stay flat, so the shock is modest. The AUD indication, GI/pancreatic MDL with a bellwether, oral amycretin parity, 0mg culture, the Pentagon programme and 'unrecognised' personality layer are all present. mechanism: most changes have chains (tariffs to gray prices to TrumpRx pills; FDA label language to litigation), but the Tennessee law's speed, the Medicare enrolment jump and the quick EMA label change (claims 1–3) are asserted more than shown. magnitude: all figures sit inside the envelope (19.4% on drug, 27.5% ever) and reconcile. The age and income checks, the 52.0M payer mix, the 33% cycling arithmetic, the Medicare $6.5B, Medicaid $3.2B/$2.1B and TRICARE $0.28B all multiply out, and approval timings of 16 and 17 months respect the 12-month rule.
rationale.generativity: The Marcus Bell scene shows rather than explains: the weigh-in, the pen that reports to the tablet, the half-eaten potatoes, the 0mg church potluck, the mother on Medicaid and gray-market pills, and the Fireball he did not think about. Together with the 0mg supper clubs, the MDL lawyers and the police and trucker programmes, it implies many characters and scenes. The ending's 'growing up' line closes the interior-life thread.
